title: Ptolemy, Geographia III.8: the towns and tribes of Dacia
creator: Klaudios Ptolemaios
provenance: Manuscript tradition; editio princeps with maps, Bologna 1477
historical_context: The earliest systematic account of Dacia as a coordinate list rather than a picture
notes: Ancient testimony about the province's extent, and the thing every later reconstruction claims to restore. It is evidence about the second century and about Ptolemy's method, and about nothing after that.

title: Ortelius, Daciarum Moesiarumque vetus descriptio
creator: Abraham Ortelius
provenance: The Parergon, the historical supplement to the Theatrum
historical_context: Renaissance antiquarianism restoring an ancient province from the authors, four centuries after it ceased to exist
notes: A reconstruction, not a survey: evidence of how 1595 read the ancient authors. Recorded as contextual rather than authoritative for exactly that reason.

title: Tabula Imperii Romani, sheets L-34 and L-35
creator: International committee under the Union Academique Internationale
provenance: Published national volumes of the international series
historical_context: The twentieth-century scholarly mapping of the Roman province, and the baseline most later work inherits
citation: Tabula Imperii Romani L-34 (1968) and L-35 (1969)
notes: Cited, not reproduced: the volumes are in copyright. This is the reconstruction the Roman baseline layer follows, which is why it belongs in the reception corpus as well as in the GIS citations.

title: Interwar Romanian national cartography of Dacian continuity
creator: pending
historical_context: The interwar state's use of Roman and Dacian antiquity to underwrite the frontiers of 1920
notes: The class is real and the essay needs it; no individual sheet has been selected, and none may be named from recollection. A specific artefact must be identified in a holding institution, dated, and rights-assessed before it can leave class_only.

title: Late-communist protochronist mapping of Dacian antiquity
creator: pending
historical_context: State-sponsored antiquity in the 1970s and 1980s, in which Dacian descent carried official weight
notes: Evidence about the state that produced it and about nothing before it. As with the interwar class, no individual item is named here: naming one from memory is precisely the failure this corpus is built to prevent.

title: Unsourced maps of Dacia circulating online
creator: pending
historical_context: Contemporary reception, in which maps with no stated source circulate as though they were evidence
notes: A class the essay must describe without amplifying. Any item drawn from it stays a reference artefact whatever its apparent detail: an unidentified creator and an unstated source are what make it reception rather than evidence.
